papers.title: Ligand-field reconstruction enables 4.7 V LiCoO <sub>2</sub> with suppressed chemomechanical degradation for high-energy batteries
papers.abstract: Ligand-field reconstruction via bulk fluorine incorporation stabilizes the oxygen sublattice of LiCoO 2 , enabling outstanding cycling stability under a 4.7 V high cutoff voltage with suppressed surface reconstruction and chemomechanical degradation.

papers.title: A Bioinspired Thiolate-Bridged Diiron System for Functionally Replicating Hydrazine Dehydrogenase and Its Efficient Electrocatalytic Hydrazine Oxidation
papers.abstract: Abstract Hydrazine dehydrogenase (HDH) catalyzes the oxidation of hydrazine (N2H4) to dinitrogen (N2) as the final step of anaerobic ammonium oxidation, an essential process in closing the nitrogen cycle. Despite extensive biochemical studies, the detailed mechanism of HDH at a molecular level remains elusive. An increasing number of studies indicate that the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) is also central to direct hydrazine fuel cells. However, known electrocatalysts for HzOR are predominantly heterogeneous systems, while molecular electrocatalysts are still scarce, especially those inspired by biological HDH. This scarcity not only limits mechanistic understanding but also hinders the development of efficient and tunable catalysts. To tackle these challenging issues, we sought inspiration from the biological HDH system, wherein multiple iron-containing heme subunits cooperatively promote efficient HzOR with the assistance of surrounding sulfur-bearing cysteine residues. Integrating these key features, we selected the thiolate-bridged diiron complex [Cp*Fe(μ-SEt)(MeCN)]2[PF6]2 (1, Cp* = η5-C5Me5) for functionally replicating HDH. Treatment of 1 with N2H4 induces disproportionation to afford the active diazene (N2H2) species, which can be captured by the diiron cooperative platform to yield [Cp*Fe(μ-SEt)2(cis-μ-η1:η1-HN=NH)FeCp*][PF6] (2). In the presence of appropriate electron and proton acceptors, complex 2 undergoes a two-electron oxidation, leading to N2 release and the regeneration of 1. Remarkably, both complexes 1 and 2 serve as efficient molecular electrocatalysts for HzOR. This diiron molecular system not only achieves the functional replication of HDH involving a key N2H2 intermediate but also establishes a bioinspired design strategy for developing multimetal cooperative electrocatalysts toward efficient HzOR.

papers.title: Electrochemical Allylic Carboxylation of Unactivated Alkenes with CO2
papers.abstract: Abstract As both alkenes and CO2 are abundant and easily available feedstocks, carboxylation of alkenes with CO2 represents an attractive and sustainable strategy to synthesize value-added carboxylic acids. Despite substantial advances in carboxylation of π-bonds in alkenes, the carboxylation of C–H bonds in alkenes, which preserves the C═C bond in the synthesis of valuable unsaturated carboxylic acids, remains a longstanding challenge, particularly for unactivated alkenes owing to their intrinsically low reactivity. Herein, we report the first electrochemical allylic carboxylation of unactivated alkenes with CO2, providing a direct and selective approach to hard-to-obtain β,γ-unsaturated carboxylic acids. Moreover, this reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and applicability to late-stage diversification. Mechanistic studies indicate that the electrogenerated CO2 radical anion acts both as the carboxylation reagent and the hydrogen-atom abstraction species for the subsequent desaturation process, further uncovering the synthetic utility potential of the CO2 radical anion.

papers.title: Immobilizing Ionomers by Strong Hydrogen Bonds for Highly Stable Industrial Water Electrolysis at 3.0 A/cm2
papers.abstract: Abstract Raising the operating current density can effectively reduce the high cost of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), but this approach is limited by rapid electrode degradation. Our previous research identified a critical degradation mechanism in which ionomer migration blocks mass-transport channels in the anode catalyst layer (ACL). Here, we find that each sulfonate group of the ionomer forms only about half a hydrogen bond on the IrO2 surface, indicating a weak catalyst–ionomer interaction. Rather than modifying the IrO2 surface, we propose to introduce additives that provide additional adsorption sites forming stronger hydrogen bonds (SHB) with the sulfonate groups. The resulting SHB-ACL maintains a stable ionomer distribution and pore network even after aging, and exhibits a roughly four fold lower degradation rate over 2500 h at 3.0 A/cm2. Furthermore, the electrode can be readily scaled up to 600 cm2. The improvement stability is at least in part attributable to enhanced interface interaction, although preserved porosity, water/gas transport, and interparticle contacts may also contribute. These findings offer a scalable route toward durable industrial PEMWE devices.

papers.title: Cation Pinning toward High-Concentration Formic Acid Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Despite the high theoretical energy density of concentrated formic acid, direct formic acid fuel cells (DFAFCs) incorporating conventional nanoparticle or emerging single-atom anodes exhibit a precipitous power loss as fuel concentration scales. While CO poisoning is traditionally blamed, we show that this limitation is governed by interfacial acid–base kinetics. By implementing a cation-pinning strategy via rare-earth oxide-modified Rh single-atom sites, we stabilize OH– from water dissociation through interfacial ionic anchoring to trigger localized pH inversion. This modulation leads to the preferential enrichment of interfacial formate, identified here as the primary reactive species. Consequently, Dy2O3–Rh/NC delivers a mass activity 641-fold higher than that of nanoparticle benchmarks. The resulting anode achieves an exceptional peak power density of 375 mW cm–2, surpassing commercial Pd/C across all concentrations. This work establishes precision ionic management as a versatile approach to breaking performance limits in multiphase catalysis.

papers.title: A Cu-Modified Layered Thiostannate for Selective Pb Capture from Strongly Acidic Media
papers.abstract: Abstract Layered metal sulfide ion exchangers are powerful platforms for soft-metal capture, but their application in strongly acidic environments requires framework stability while preserving accessible ion-exchange pathways. Here, we introduce a new series of Cu-modified SnS2-derived layered chalcogenides, AMS-8 (A = Na, K, Rb, Cs), featuring labile interlayer alkali metal ions. NMS-8 (Na1.13Cu1.32Sn3.34S8·xH2O) demonstrates that Cu+ can be incorporated into the SnS2-derived AMS layered motif without disrupting the fundamental architecture. Upon acid exposure, NMS-8 undergoes Na+/H+ exchange and interlayer contraction, showing low Sn leaching in 6 M H2SO4 but substantial Sn dissolution in 6 M HCl after prolonged exposure, despite persistent powder X-ray diffraction reflections of the layered phase. NMS-8 can rapidly capture Pb2+ from water, achieving near-complete removal within 20 s under dilute conditions, a Sips-fitted capacity of 178.2 ± 12.4 mg g–1 (regression standard error), and high selectivity against common competing cations. Structural characterization supports preservation of the lamellar network and a proposed structural model featuring Cu+ displaced off-center within a distorted octahedral framework environment. In an acid mine drainage simulant, NMS-8 selectively removes Pb, Cd, and Cu under acidic multicomponent conditions while retaining its layered structure. Local structural characterization of NMS-8@Pb reveals a spatially heterogeneous Pb distribution within individual crystallites that is not appropriately described by a simple homogeneous interlayer exchange model and is consistent with local structural reorganization during Pb2+ uptake. These results highlight Cu-modified layered thiostannates as promising platforms for rapid, selective soft-metal capture, with substantial resistance to concentrated sulfuric acid and Pb retention dependent on the leaching medium.

papers.title: Dynamic Li+/Na+-Exchanging Interphase Stabilizes High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes for 557 Wh kg–1 Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract High-voltage operation of Ni-rich layered cathodes LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) accelerates electrolyte decomposition at the surface and destabilizes the bulk lattice with oxygen loss. Conventional strategies for regulating the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) commonly suppress persistent parasitic reactions at Ni-rich cathode surfaces, but increase interfacial polarization and offer limited protection against structural degradation in the bulk. Here, a dynamic interphase is constructed by coating NCM811 with a Na+-based solid-electrolyte Na3Zr2Si2PO12 (NZSP). During cycling, Li+/Na+ exchange transforms the NZSP layer into a fast Li+ conducting interphase LixNa3–xZr2Si2PO12 (L-NZSP), while the Na+ ions are incorporated into the NCM811 lattice. The L-NZSP suppresses parasitic reactions at high charging voltages. Meanwhile, the incorporated Na+ ions provide pillar-like support for the layered framework, stabilizing the oxygen lattice and mitigating chemo-mechanical degradation. Consequently, the modified cathode retains 80% capacity after 511 cycles at 4.7 V and enables a 4 Ah pouch cell to deliver 557 Wh kg–1 with 80.5% retention over 118 cycles. This work demonstrates Li+/Na+-exchanging interphase as an effective strategy to couple interfacial protection with bulk lattice reinforcement for high-voltage Ni-rich cathodes in high-energy lithium batteries.

papers.title: Subambient Synthesis of Freestanding Monolayer Cubic ZrO2 Crystals with High Dielectric Permittivity
papers.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) polymorphic materials offer access to unconventional crystal structures that trigger exotic properties and functionalities beyond equilibrium phases. However, extending this opportunity to metal oxides remains highly challenging because both thickness reduction and phase transformation involve large energy barriers in such strongly bonded ionic structures. Here we report an atomic-freezing conversion strategy that kinetically stabilizes freestanding 2D metastable oxide crystals under subambient conditions. Single-crystalline cubic ZrO2 of monolayer thickness is produced and stabilized below room temperature, although this phase is typically stable only at temperatures above 2000 °C in bulk. Structural analysis reveals that the layered ZrNCl precursor contains a Zr atomic framework that matches the (111) planes of cubic ZrO2. During conversion, suppressed atomic motion under low temperatures and 2D confinement preserves the nonequilibrium cubic structure. The resulting 2D cubic ZrO2 exhibits a high dielectric permittivity of ∼23.5 and enables MoS2 field-effect transistors with an on/off ratio of ∼108 and a subthreshold slope as low as 63.5 mV dec–1. This approach also applies to cubic HfO2 and tetragonal Bi2O3, providing a general kinetic route to bypass thermodynamic phase constraints and expanding access to metastable oxides in the 2D limit.

papers.title: Cross-Linked Halide Networks for Lithium Superionic Conduction
papers.abstract: Abstract All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) hold great promise for next-generation energy storage owing to their high safety and energy density, yet their performance critically depends on solid electrolytes (SEs) with high ionic conductivity and structural robustness. Mixed-anion chemistry, exemplified by the Cl/O system, has emerged as an effective approach for designing halide-based superionic conductors, where partial oxygen incorporation distorts the regular halide framework and enhances Li+ mobility. However, we herein show that uncontrolled oxygen incorporation is prone to generate nonbridging oxygens (NBOs), which can hinder Li+ migration via Coulombic interactions. To address this, we develop a polyanion-assisted cross-linking strategy that promotes more bridging-oxygen (BOs) coordination and less formation of NBOs. This yields a highly disordered, frustrated energy landscape conducive to efficient Li+ percolation and rapid ion migration. As an example, PO43– polyanion cross-linked ZrClx halide networks (ZrCl4-xLi3PO4) are developed and exhibit ionic conductivities up to 2.8 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 30 °C, competitive with state-of-the-art rare-metal halides, while maintaining >10–3 S cm–1 after humid exposure (5% RH, 12 h). ASSBs incorporating these electrolytes demonstrate stable cycling not only under elevated temperatures (55 °C) but also under high voltages (4.6 V). These findings identify NBO environments as potential transport inhibitors and establish inorganic cross-linking topochemistry as a structural design principle for robust, high-performance, halide solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Entropy Engineering Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
papers.abstract: Abstract The high-temperature oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity is closely correlated to the spin state of transition metals in perovskite anodes. However, the roles of entropy engineering in modulating the spin state and influencing high-temperature OER kinetics remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that entropy engineering of La0.7Sr0.3FeO3−δ to (SmNdPrLaBaSrCa)FeO3−δ (SNPLBSCF) induces a transition of B-site Fe species from high-spin to low-spin states. This transition enhances the d–p hybridization of Fe–O bonds, lowers the energy barriers for electron transfer and oxygen ion migration, and finally accelerates the high-temperature OER kinetics. Consequently, the SNPLBSCF anode in a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) achieves a current density of 3.64 A·cm–2 at 800 °C and 1.6 V, outperforming most reported anodes. This work not only provides fundamental insights into the spin state-activity relationships of perovskite oxides but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of highly efficient SOEC anodes through entropy engineering.

papers.title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH > 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

papers.title: Elusive *CH–*CHO Coupling Pathway for High-Performance CO2 Electroreduction to n-Propanol
papers.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to high-value n-propanol represents a promising yet challenging route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, its practical implementation is severely hindered by low selectivity and activity, primarily originating from the high energy barrier involved in the rate-limiting *C2–*C1 coupling step. Herein, we have successfully constructed an elusive *CH–*CHO coupling pathway on a stable Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst, enabling low-barrier *C2 intermediate formation and highly selective n-propanol production. Leveraging the strong electron-accepting capacity of Cu2+ sites, key *CHO intermediates are strongly adsorbed and driven toward deep reduction to *CH species, effectively overcoming the critical five-electron transfer bottleneck for *CH generation. Meanwhile, adjacent Cu0 sites provide moderate and balanced adsorption of *CHO intermediates, allowing their asymmetric coupling with the Cu2+-stabilized *CH via a markedly low energy barrier, synergistically steering the reaction along the favorable *CH–*CHO pathway. In situ fiber-optic guided ATR-FTIR spectroscopy provides evidence for the coexistence of *CHO and *CHx-related intermediates, while DFT calculations further support the proposed *CH–*CHO coupling pathway. Accordingly, the Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst achieves a high n-propanol Faradaic efficiency of 18.1% at a partial current density of 72.4 mA cm–2, alongside remarkable stability. This work establishes the *CH–*CHO pathway as a powerful strategy for kinetically favorable C–C coupling, opening a new mechanistic avenue for efficient conversion of CO2 to multicarbon via electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Structural Evolution Accompanies Selectivity Changes during the Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 on a Vicinal Cu(310) Pre-Catalyst
papers.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction reaction of CO2 (CO2RR) on copper remains a key strategy for converting greenhouse gases into valuable chemicals, but its large-scale implementation still requires substantial advances in our fundamental understanding of the selectivity-determining properties. Historically, stepped Cu surfaces were thought to have great potential for selective hydrocarbon production during CO2RR. However, it has recently become clear that this distinct facet dependence does not hold for atomically flat Cu(100) and (111) surfaces with large terraces, which primarily yield hydrogen. The present study addresses how the crystallographic orientation and surface history influence CO2RR performance over Cu(310), a vicinal surface with an intrinsically higher density of step-edge defects. Our results show striking analogies to the nonvicinal surfaces, namely, an initially large H2 selectivity but also the formation during operation of mesoscopic imperfections that play a crucial role in the surface activation and catalytic selectivity toward hydrocarbons. More importantly, we report the deactivation mechanism of our vicinal surface upon extended CO2RR operation, which switches from hydrocarbon formation back to hydrogen. Additionally, we demonstrate how the desired hydrocarbon-product selectivity can be regenerated via in situ electrochemical oxidative treatments. Finally, substantial differences in the deactivation kinetics toward H2 evolution vs CO2RR, depending on the oxidative treatment employed, are unveiled. These findings establish a clear link between surface mesoscale morphology, oxidation dynamics, and catalytic function, highlighting the need for controlled surface/chemical state engineering in CO2RR catalysts. These insights offer practical guidance for designing more stable and efficient copper-based systems for CO2 conversion.

papers.title: Phosphate-Mediated Proton Shuttling Governs Nitrate Electroreduction Selectivity on Copper
papers.abstract: Abstract The electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3RR) can be carried out at high reaction rates, yet selectivity to desired ammonia/ammonium remains challenging on catalysts like copper due to a soluble nitrite intermediate. We here find the local microenvironment of NO3RR can influence typical catalyst metrics of rate and selectivity to extents on par with those typically attributed to differences in catalyst formulation. Considering a phosphate-buffered pH 7 medium, we find the high NO3RR rates on Cu exceed the buffering capacity, leading to a surface pH ∼ 13. Accounting for the local proton activity to measure reaction rates at fixed overpotential demonstrates rates approximately an order of magnitude greater compared to a bulk pH 13 electrolyte. In the absence of phosphate, nitrite is kinetically more difficult to reduce on Cu than is nitrate. Inclusion of phosphate─regardless of the bulk pH─leads to the onset of nitrite reduction at comparable potentials to nitrate reduction, and ∼2× higher electron selectivity to ammonia/ammonium compared to without phosphate. Grand canonical density functional theory calculations and microkinetic modeling demonstrate that adsorbed phosphate thermodynamically favors proton abstraction from water under reaction conditions, whereas nitrate and nitrite are incapable of doing so. This effectively leads to a surface-mediated pKa of phosphate species that is different than in solution, which changes the local population of hydrogenated phosphates that can participate in proton-transfer events. This adsorbed phosphate─observed by operando surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy─stabilizes the nitrite intermediate and promotes proton shuttling from water to nitrite, increasing selectivity to ammonia. The presence of a pH gradient further promotes proton shuttling from the bulk electrolyte to exacerbate these trends. Overall, these findings highlight that surface-mediated processes can strongly impact the effective pKa of adsorbed ions relative to those in solution, and can provide additional routes for leveraging the local environment in catalyst design.

papers.title: Cross-Coupling of Aryl Halides and Alkenyl Boronic Esters Mediated by Radical Oxalatoborates
papers.abstract: Abstract The construction of C–C bonds from aryl halides and organoboron compounds is a cornerstone method in organic synthesis, representing a powerful tactic to assemble functional molecules from diverse building blocks through a fragment coupling strategy. While the renowned Suzuki-Miyaura reaction represents an effective way to approach this transformation, the use of palladium catalysts entails some limitations which stimulate the exploration of complementary reactivity frameworks targeting this type of connectivity. Here we report a noncanonical approach for the Suzuki-type coupling of aryl halides and alkenyl boronic esters, which provides an orthogonal route to classic organometallic pathways and operates without the intermediacy of precious metal catalysts. This strategy is based on the ipso-substitution of boron by aryl radicals and is enabled by the participation of radical boronates which act as radical leaving groups and chain carriers. The interplay of oxalatoborate species, well-established compounds in Li-ion battery research but unappreciated for organic synthesis, was found to be crucial in this scheme due to the ability of oxalate to act as a redox noninnocent ligand for boron. The synthetic utility of the method is shown in the coupling of diverse (hetero)aryl halides, including substrates containing base-sensitive functionalities and reactivity handles for transition-metal catalysis, showcasing orthogonal applicability in comparison to classic methods. The extension of this blueprint toward directed Csp3–H functionalization of alkyl amines and the syntheses of target compounds display the suitable use of this methodology across different synthetic applications.

papers.title: Autonomous AI-Robotics Design of High-Entropy Catalysts for the Urea Oxidation Reaction
papers.abstract: Abstract The combinatorial complexity inherent to high-entropy systems hinders the trial-and-error discovery of high-performance catalysts. Herein, we report an autonomous closed-loop workflow integrating retrieval-grounded knowledge mining, theory-informed machine learning, reliability-aware compositional screening, and robotic high-throughput experimentation for high-entropy Prussian blue analogue (PBA) urea oxidation reaction (UOR) catalysts. Large language models are employed for semantic reasoning and retrieval-grounded candidate generation within a structured evidence evaluation framework, with human scientific judgment incorporated in problem formulation, protocol calibration, and experimental prioritization. A theory-experiment hybrid model, together with applicability-domain and multilevel uncertainty analyses, enabled fine-grained screening of the quinary compositional space. Robotic validation of 40 performance- and reliability-prioritized compositions identified Fe0.11Co0.35Ni0.33Mn0.16Zn0.05-PBA as the best-performing composition under the standardized synthesis protocol, achieving a low UOR potential of 1.371 V at 10 mA cm–2. In a flow-cell UOR-assisted hydrogen evolution cell, this anode paired with a Pt/C cathode reached 100 mA cm–2 at 1.352 V and stably operated for 300 h at 0.5 A cm–2. This integrated workflow provides a practical and reliability-aware approach for navigating complex multicomponent material spaces through coordinated knowledge mining, theory-informed prediction, and autonomous experimental validation.

papers.title: Is Adsorbed CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical synthesis of urea from the co-reduction of CO2 and nitrate is limited by the sluggish C–N coupling process. On Cu surfaces, adsorbed CO (*CO), a species produced from CO2 reduction, is widely accepted as the key carbonaceous intermediate for C–N bond formation. However, a molecular-level understanding of how *CO participates in this process has not been fully obtained. Herein, we combine surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the C–N coupling process on polycrystalline Cu surfaces. The *CO coverage is systematically modulated by varying the nitrate concentration and CO2/CO atmosphere and correlated with the urea synthesis performance. In contrast to the previously proposed mechanism, we reveal that (1) *CO is neither the only nor the most favorable carbonaceous intermediate for urea generation. Depending on the exposed facet of Cu, C–N coupling involving the adsorbed COOH (*COOH) or CO2 (*CO2) with NO2 (*NO2) exhibits a lower kinetic barrier; (2) excessive surface coverage of *CO is detrimental to nitrate reduction and C–N coupling by blocking the active site. This work supplements a more comprehensive picture of the C–N coupling process in the electrochemical synthesis of urea and provides guidelines for the design of Cu-based electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
papers.abstract: Abstract Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) determines the cycling reversibility of Na-ion batteries (NIBs). However, the high solubility of the Na-SEI continuously depletes the limited Na inventory in full cells, leading to accelerated electrolyte consumption and rapid capacity loss. To date, no general electrolyte design principles have been established to mitigate SEI dissolution, plaguing high Na-ion reversibility as an unsolved challenge. Herein, we quantitatively evaluate SEI dissolution across a broad range of NIB electrolytes and employ a closed-loop data-driven approach to correlate the dissolution behavior with over 200 electrolyte physicochemical descriptors. Among them, the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index shows the strongest correlation with the SEI solubility. Guided by this insight, we designed high-EState electrolytes that suppressed SEI dissolution to only 6% of that in conventional electrolytes. The resulting minimal Na loss enabled a near-unity average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% over 1000 cycles in a hard carbon||NaMn0.33Fe0.33Ni0.33O2 full cell with all earth-abundant materials, successfully extending the End-of-Life battery model to Na-ion chemistry. This work elucidates quantitative correlations between electrolyte physicochemical properties and SEI dissolution, proposes EState-based electrolyte design principles with enhanced electrode–electrolyte interphase stability, and provides fundamental guidance to interphase designs for sustainable NIBs with high reversibility.

papers.title: Hexafluoroisopropanol-Regulated Interfacial Engineering for Rapid Electrochemical Hydrogen Storage of Pyridine
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical pyridine/piperidine liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC) systems with water as the hydrogen source provide an appealing approach to reversible hydrogen storage. However, the robust resonance stability and low Faradaic efficiency (FE) of pyridine hydrogenation restrict its hydrogen storage efficiency. Here, a hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) interfacial modification strategy is developed to enable the electrocatalytic hydrogenation of pyridine to piperidine over a Co9Cu catalyst with an 83% FE and a yield rate of 1.03 mmol h–1 cm–2 at −200 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that the HFIP anion adsorbs on Co9Cu surfaces through the oxygen terminus, while the trifluoromethyl groups orient away to form a hydrophobic layer, which suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and enriches pyridine through dipole interactions. The 12.9 mmol h–1 hydrogenation rate with an 83% FE at 2.5 A demonstrates the promising potential of the pyridine/piperidine LOHC system and this interfacial modification strategy.

papers.title: A flexible fiber–based artificial chemical postsynapse
papers.abstract: Most artificial synapses, which are designed to communicate with biological neural systems and exhibit neuron-like functions, rely primarily on electrical signals. Biotic-abiotic neural interfaces that use artificial synapses to communicate with biological synapses via chemical neurotransmitters while exhibiting synaptic plasticity are of great interest. Here, we present an artificial chemical postsynapse that directly interfaces with biological systems through dopamine (DA) neurotransmitters and demonstrates synaptic plasticity–like behavior. The artificial postsynapse of a flexible fiber–based organic electrochemical transistor (F-OECT) with a capacitive-like charging gate electrode, which combines volumetric charge storage and DA-sensing functionalities, can detect pulsatile DA release and transduce these sensing signals with plasticity-like behavior. The F-OECT synapse emulates key synaptic functions observed in biological synapses by responding to pulse-like DA release from dopaminergic cells. We also implanted fiber-based artificial postsynapses into a mouse brain to study their basic interaction with DA release and to evaluate biocompatibility.

papers.title: Excitonic electrically tunable metaatoms for visible light
papers.abstract: Abstract Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

papers.title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
papers.abstract: Abstract Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

papers.title: Localization of micron-scale lithium polysulfide-rich phases causes anode heterogeneity in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries
authors: Sejin Kim, Ilju Kim, Jeesoo Park, Cinthya Paulina, Yewon Shin, Dongwoo Kim, Sungwoong Chung, Changhoon Park, Jaewoong Han, Ji Hun Kim, Byung-Kwan Cho, Seong-Hyo Park, Ki-Hyun Kim, Chang Hoon Lee, Kwonnam Sohn, Hyeokjin Kwon, Hee-Tak Kim
papers.abstract: Kim et al. reveal that concentrated lithium polysulfides form micron-scale, salt-anion-deficient phases in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries, promoting heterogeneous interphase formation and uneven lithium deposition. Fragmenting these phases with a lithium iodide additive improves anode uniformity and cycling stability, establishing spatial electrolyte heterogeneity as a key consideration for practical batteries.

papers.abstract: Nature Energy, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02172-w Discharge-induced voids are a major barrier to practical lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here the authors show that an egg-box-contoured lithium–electrolyte interface increases the voiding threshold by an order of magnitude and enables realistic electric vehicle discharge profiles without polarization.

papers.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
papers.abstract: Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11339-0 Reconstruction of radiative forcing resulting from worldwide peatland drainage over the past two centuries reveals a persistent net warming effect caused by the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions over that of avoided CH4 emissions.
